_comment_purpose: Lane C, C-03: put Cosys-AirSim into PX4 EXTERNAL-AUTOPILOT mode so PX4 SITL flies the
vehicle over the MAVLink Simulator API, while PX4's own uxrce_dds_client exposes the
SAME /fmu/* topics Lane A produces. MAVLink drives the sim physics handshake; XRCE-DDS
drives the autonomy code. Coupling: lane-c-topic-parity.
Passed with --settings rather than dropped in ~/Documents/AirSim/, so the config is a
reviewable repo artifact instead of per-machine state.
_comment_clocktype: SteppableClock is required for lockstep: AirSim advances the clock one step per sensor
update, so PX4's clock tracks the sim regardless of render latency. Without it a slow
UE frame trips PX4 SITL timeouts - the documented fragility of this integration.
CONFIRMED DEAD 2026-08-01: the LockStep flag below IS SILENTLY INEFFECTIVE. In the
vendored tree, initialize() sets lock_step_enabled_ (MavLinkMultirotorApi.hpp:66) and
then openAllConnections() clears it TWICE before returning - via close()->disconnect()
->resetState() (:957) and directly (:992) - and nothing sets it again. So the guard at
:1613 can never pass and 'Enabling lockstep mode' can never be logged. It never was:
zero occurrences across a full session, while other addStatusMessage output from the
same path did appear. Measured RTF 0.9193 (10.960 s sim over 11.922 s wall), i.e.
tracking wall time rather than stepping. LockStep is left true deliberately - it states
the INTENT and will start working the moment the vendor patch lands (C-09). Until then,
treat every Lane C timing number as free-running. See versions.lock

_comment_transport: TCP, not serial: PX4 dials OUT as a TCP client to 4560+instance while AirSim is the
server. TCP support was added to PX4 in 1.9.2 specifically because lockstep needs
guaranteed delivery. Verified present in PX4 v1.16.0 at
_comment_gpulidar_AND_WHY_THIS_COMMENT_I: SensorType 8 = GPULidar (SensorBase::SensorType: 6 is the CPU Lidar, 8 is the GPU one).
GPU-LiDAR is a large part of why Lane C replaced Lane B: tunable noise and ground-truth
labels at a point count a CPU lidar cannot reach.
The gpulidar entry is ADDED to the four sensors below, not replacing them.
THIS COMMENT LIVES AT VEHICLE LEVEL ON PURPOSE. loadSensorSettings iterates the KEYS of
the Sensors block and reads SensorType off each one, so a _comment_ key placed inside
Sensors is parsed as a sensor with SensorType 0 - not a valid enum value. Only per-sensor
_comment fields nested INSIDE a sensor object (see barometer) are safe.
Settings are modest deliberately: the lidar shares a GPU with the renderer, and lockstep
is confirmed dead, so a heavy sensor degrades the sim rather than slowing it deterministically.
_comment_sensors_MUST_BE_COMPLETE: A Sensors block REPLACES the defaults, it does not extend them - AirSimSettings.hpp
createDefaultSensorSettings is only called 'when none specified in json'. An earlier
version of this file listed ONLY the barometer, which left the vehicle with no IMU,
no GPS and no magnetometer. PX4 armed anyway and then auto-disarmed:
Preflight Fail: height estimate not stable
The controller saw 'armed' and then timed out in takeoff, which looks like a control
bug and is not one. All four multirotor defaults are therefore listed explicitly.

_comment: PressureFactorSigma tweak from upstream's PX4 docs: reduces barometer drift so
GPS lock and EKF2 convergence happen quickly instead of stalling the run.

_comment_cameras: C-04. Without this block the vehicle has NO cameras as far as settings are concerned,
so the ROS 2 wrapper publishes no image or camera_info topics at all - which is why
the first C-04 topic sweep found 14 topics and no imagery. The UE pawn does carry
default cameras (simGetImages over RPC works on front_center etc.), but the wrapper
enumerates vehicle_setting->cameras, and loadCameraSettings starts with cameras.clear().
Unlike the Sensors block above, adding this REPLACES an empty default, so nothing is
(ImageCaptureBase::ImageType). 640x480 rather than the 256x144 default: the default is
too small for perception and was only ever adequate for a debug view.

_comment_image_quality: These three keys are why Lane C imagery stopped looking washed out. Measured
2026-08-03 against Unreal's own HighResShot of the SAME camera actor at the
same transform; with them the two agree to 1.15 of 255, without them AirSim is
up to 8.6 brighter and 20.3 flatter. All three apply to ImageType 0 only.
LumenGIEnable / LumenReflectionEnable: these do NOT merely skip Lumen when
false. PIPCamera.cpp:701-715 takes an else branch that FORCES
DynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod::None and ReflectionMethod::None, so a world
authored for Lumen (any modern UE5 environment) renders with GI and reflections
off through the capture path while its own viewport keeps them.
ForceUpdate: cameras start as nodisplay, so bCaptureEveryFrame is false
(PIPCamera.cpp:186-188, :455-459) and the capture renders one shot per request.
bAlwaysPersistRenderingState is true, so the temporal history buffer exists but
nothing accumulates into it and TSR/TAA never converges - which shows up as
colour fringing on foliage. Setting it true (-> setCameraTypeUpdate(Scene,
false), PIPCamera.cpp:730) cut high-frequency noise 13.9% at 1080p with no
measurable frame-rate cost. A Lumen-off control showed it is specifically
denoising Lumen's stochastic GI sampling, so it pairs with the two keys above.
Upstream flags it 'costly for performance!' and the cost scales with the number
of ENABLED cameras - see lane-c-sensor-rates for the measured rates here.

_comment: DepthPlanar, not DepthPerspective: planar depth is the Z-distance in the
camera frame, which is what depth_image_proc and cuVSLAM expect. Perspective
depth is ray length and would silently bias any point cloud built from it.

_comment_params_deliberately_absent: Upstream's PX4 example sets NAV_RCL_ACT=0 and NAV_DLL_ACT=0 to disable the RC-loss
and datalink-loss failsafes. NOT done here, deliberately.
Lane A leaves the GCS-datalink check ENFORCED (NAV_DLL_ACT=2, set by the x500
airframe) and satisfies it with a real QGroundControl service, because PX4 refusing
to arm without a datalink is a property of the real aircraft too. Disabling it in
Lane C would make the two lanes diverge exactly where sim-to-real parity matters,
and would hide an arming failure that the real Pixhawk 6C would still have.
Consequence: arming in Lane C will need a datalink the same way Lane A does. That is
the intended behaviour, not an oversight.
